q: Where exactly does the ~15% gap in Q_factory originate? Our closed-form estimate using the paper's own per-magic-state spacetime overhead (5.35e5 qubit-rounds at p_g=1e-4) yields Q_fact=5.35e6 data qubits, but the paper's Table I reports 6.30e6 -- a 17.7% upward adjustment. The paper attributes it to iterative balanced-investment surface-code distance optimization plus rounding, but publishes no line-item decomposition.
basis: Observed 5.35e6 vs paper's 6.30e6 in our reproduction (ratio 0.849). Paper's Table I footnote mentions the doubling for ancilla stabilizer qubits and the iterative optimizer but does not decompose the residual overhead.
next_steps: Re-implement the paper's Sec. IV balanced-investment iterative optimizer (choose surface-code distance d_i separately at each distillation level so that d_i suppresses the injected error to 10x below the input error required by level i+1), and see if that alone recovers the 6.30e6 number. If not, the remaining gap is ancilla-for-stabilizer bookkeeping.

q: Does the 2/3-visibility factor observed in our raw noise measurement generalize to more realistic T-gate injection noise models? The paper's assumption epsilon_in = 0.4 * p_g implicitly encodes a specific mapping (Li 2015) between physical two-qubit gate error and injected magic-state error. How sensitive is the Table I factory footprint to the 0.4 prefactor being e.g. 0.3 or 0.5 in a realistic ion-trap or superconducting implementation?
basis: Our Qiskit MC fit gave slope 0.98 for raw error vs injected p, consistent with the depolarizing model, but that number is model-dependent. The paper uses 0.4 as a single scalar with no error bars.
next_steps: Rerun the paper's balanced-investment optimizer with epsilon_in = c*p_g for c in {0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0} and plot Q_factory(c). Determines whether the 6.3M-qubit headline is robust or fragile to injection-noise-model choice.

q: Is the paper's assumption t_meas/ff = 0.1 * t_sc architecture-realistic beyond distributed ion traps? The 11-hour figure for 1000-bit Shor at t_sc=1e-5 s hinges on this ratio. Modern superconducting demonstrators report t_meas and t_sc closer than 1:10. If t_meas/ff ~ t_sc the factoring runtime blows up by 10x to ~4.6 days.
basis: Our reproduction of 11.11 h exactly matched the paper -- BECAUSE we used the same 0.1 assumption. The scaling is completely linear in this ratio, so the assumption is the load-bearing part of the runtime claim.
next_steps: Survey 2020-2026 experimental papers (Google Sycamore/Willow, IBM Heron/Condor, IonQ, Quantinuum) for measured t_meas vs. t_sc; produce a sensitivity table of Shor runtime vs. this ratio. Cross-check against arXiv:2207.06431 (Google surface-code logical qubit, a sibling QC-200 paper).

q: How does the O'Gorman-Campbell 6.3M-qubit estimate compare to more recent Litinski-style 'game-of-surface-codes' resource estimates (2019)? Litinski removes the monolithic-factory assumption and sprinkles distillation into idle spacetime. On the same 1000-bit Shor benchmark at p_g=1e-4, does Litinski's estimate match, undercut, or exceed O'Gorman-Campbell's 6.3e6?
basis: The paper is from 2016 and predates the modern spacetime-tradeoff literature. Our reproduction confirms the paper's internal arithmetic but says nothing about whether the framework itself has been superseded.
next_steps: Reproduce the Litinski 2019 (arXiv:1808.02892) magic-state factory qubit budget for 1000-bit Shor at p_g=1e-4 using the same 40N^3 gate count. Compare 6.3e6 head-to-head; a 2-3x reduction would indicate O'Gorman-Campbell's numbers are now upper bounds, not state-of-the-art.

q: Does the 35 p^3 cubic law's leading-order truncation break at the boundary of the paper's operating regime? The full 15-to-1 output error is 35 p^3 + O(p^4); at p_in=1e-2 the next-order correction could contribute >=10% if the O(p^4) prefactor is not small.
basis: Our analytic reproduction used only the 35 p^3 leading term. At p_in=1e-2 we get p_out=3.5e-5, but if the next-order coefficient is 300 (plausible for a 15-choose-4 combinatorial factor) the true p_out is closer to 6.5e-5 -- a ~2x factor missing from the top end of the 15-to-1 sweep.
next_steps: Derive the O(p^4) coefficient for 15-to-1 either analytically (Bravyi-Kitaev original paper 2005) or by explicit Reed-Muller stabilizer-simulator counting in Stim. Report the crossover p_in beyond which the leading-order 35 p^3 formula misestimates by >10%; check whether any of the paper's design points sit above that crossover.
